idea: Trim-triggered verbatim re-copy
mechanism: The trimming routine stays oldest-first, but when the trim drops the message holding the task text it appends a verbatim copy of that text as a new user message at the tail. The goal therefore reappears exactly when it would otherwise vanish, lands at the end of the window [F22], and no message is ever protected, so assumptions one and two hold.
prediction: Lost-the-goal failures with task text absent (9 of 11 today [F4]) fall to near zero; long-task pass rises from 31 to 37 to 40 percent; tokens per run rise under 5 percent since a copy is added only at each trim event, typically one to three per run.
test: 12 long tasks, seeds 1 to 3, 36 runs, with the goal-present flag logged at the final step. Refuted if pass gain on the screen is under +3 points or if lost-the-goal still accounts for 4 or more of the failed runs read. Full measurement on 48 tasks, 144 runs, judged on the keep rule [F18].
source: https://www.agentpatterns.ai/instructions/event-driven-system-reminders/ (event-triggered reminders; using the trim itself as the trigger is new here)
target: ranked list, keep rule (long-task pass up, cost within 20 percent)

idea: Verbatim-quote gate on the summariser
mechanism: The summariser prompt is told to open with the task text in a quoted block, and the harness accepts the summary only if that block matches the original by exact string compare, retrying the summary once and otherwise falling back to the raw copy. This removes the mechanism that made summaries raise lost-the-goal failures in 6 of 10 cases [F14] while keeping the stale-context benefit summaries showed.
prediction: Rerunning the tried 20-step summariser with the gate turns its +3 points [F14] into +6 to +8, because stale-context gains remain and the lost-the-goal rise is removed; summary acceptance on first try is above 80 percent, so retry cost is small.
test: Same 12-task screen, two arms, gated summariser versus the recorded ungated result. Refuted if lost-the-goal failures in the gated arm still rise over baseline, or if the first-try acceptance rate is under 50 percent, which would mean the summariser cannot be trusted to quote.
target: failure link (ties the summariser's two opposite effects in [F14] to one checkable cause)

idea: Ephemeral tail reminder behind the cache point
mechanism: Before each model call the harness appends the task text as the final message of the request but never writes it to stored history, so it neither accumulates nor invalidates the cached prefix. The goal is in the chronological list for every call, always in the last position, at a per-call cost that cache pricing largely absorbs.
prediction: Same lost-the-goal reduction as the trim-triggered copy, with cost per run measured in billed tokens rising under 3 percent, and short-task pass unchanged since short runs never trim [F1].
test: 12-task screen, arm against the trim-triggered copy, logging billed and cached tokens separately. Refuted if the always-present goal lowers pass on the 12 short tasks included as a guard, or if billed tokens rise more than the stored-copy arm, which would show the cache does not absorb it.

idea: Goal-present attribution read for the model-limits section
mechanism: Every failed run in the 20-run sample read gets two new columns, goal present at the last step and goal present at the first wrong edit. Lost-the-goal failures that happen with the text in view, 2 of 11 today [F4], plus any residual after pinning, are the candidates for the model-limit list, with a stated reason per run rather than the current guess.
prediction: After pinning, remaining lost-the-goal failures split into a small goal-present group of about 2 to 3 per 40 fails that no pin can fix, and the answer can state that number with its cause rather than estimate it.
test: Apply the two columns to the 20-run reads of the baseline and of the pinned arm. Refuted if lost-the-goal failures with the goal present do not fall as a share, which would mean the taxonomy label hides a different failure, most likely a loop or stale context mislabeled.

idea: Agent restatement handshake
mechanism: On a trigger (each trim event, or every 15 steps), the harness asks the agent for a one-line restatement of the goal and compares it to the original by requirement sentence; it injects the verbatim text only when a requirement is missing. The agent proves it still holds the goal, so injection is gated by a cheap, checkable signal rather than by a timer, and the probe doubles as a drift measure the panel can see.
prediction: Restatement misses precede lost-the-goal failures in most such runs, giving a drift signal a few steps ahead as the probe paper found, but here the gate costs about 100 tokens per check instead of a trained probe; pass gain matches the trim-triggered copy at lower injected volume, under 3 percent to
test: 12-task screen with the handshake arm against the trim-triggered copy. Refuted if misses do not precede failure in at least 6 of the 9 goal-gone-type runs, or if the restatement itself drags the agent off task, visible as a pass drop on the 12 short guard tasks.
source: own (the probe idea in https://www.emergentmind.com/papers/2606.22953 is the departure point; replacing a trained probe with a self-report compared to the source is the change)
target: failure link, model limits (runs that fail with a correct restatement are model-limited)
breaks: The harness decides when the goal needs re-showing; here the agent must show it still holds the goal and the harness acts only on a mismatch.
keeps: Goal in the chronological list, positional trimming, verbatim text when injected, same 48-task and seed measurement.
kill: Restatement misses precede fewer than 6 of 9 goal-gone-type failures on the screen, or screen pass gain is under +3 points.

idea: Funded re-copy at zero window cost
mechanism: Each verbatim copy appended at the tail is paid for immediately by an extra positional trim of the oldest tool output of equal token size, so the window never grows from pinning. What is lost is the oldest tool output, which SWE-agent found is mostly noise anyway [F21], and the measured cost line of the proposal shows pinning at or near zero added tokens.
prediction: Pass gain equals the plain trim-triggered copy within seed spread, with tokens per run unchanged or lower, because the extra trim removes stale tool output that would otherwise be reprocessed on every later call.
test: 12-task screen, funded arm against the unfunded copy, logging tokens per run and stale-context failures. Refuted if stale-context failures rise, meaning the evicted tool outputs were still needed, or if tokens per run do not fall below the unfunded arm.
breaks: Re-injecting the goal must add tokens to the window; here every injected token is offset by an equal positional eviction.
keeps: Oldest-first trimming, goal as a chronological message, no protected messages, same thresholds of 100k and 80k [F9].
kill: Stale-context failures on the screen rise by 2 or more over the unfunded arm, or tokens per run are not lower.

idea: Stop-gate goal check
mechanism: Nothing is injected during the run; when the agent signals it is done, the harness appends the verbatim task text with the instruction to confirm each requirement sentence against the current repository state before stopping, allowing up to 8 more tool calls. The goal is re-shown at the single point where its absence is fatal, so cost falls only on runs that reach a stop, and the check also catches the wrong-verification endings a reader would have accepted [F7].
prediction: Lost-the-goal failures that end in a premature or off-target done fall by more than half; wrong-verification falls by 2 to 3 of 6; pass rises 5 to 8 points; tokens rise under 8 percent since most runs add fewer than 8 steps.
test: 12-task screen, stop-gate arm against baseline, counting how many stops are revoked and how many revoked runs then pass. Refuted if fewer than a quarter of revoked stops convert to passes, or if runs that hit the step cap, where no stop is signalled, hold most of the lost-the-goal failures.
target: ranked list, failure link (two failure kinds from one step)
breaks: The goal must be kept in view throughout the run; here it is shown only at the moment of stopping.
keeps: Goal as a chronological message, positional trimming, verbatim text, the agent still does the verification itself [F10], no tool or step-cap change.
kill: Fewer than 3 of the 12 screened tasks gain a pass in any seed, or more than 60 percent of lost-the-goal failures on the screen end by step cap rather than by a stop.

idea: Re-copy interval and trim-target sweep
mechanism: Once the trim-triggered copy exists, two constants decide its cost: how often a copy is added and how far the trim cuts, currently to under 80k [F9]. Cutting less deeply, to under 95k, means more frequent but smaller trims and more copies; a timer of every 10, 20 or 30 steps adds copies independent of trims. Sweeping both finds the cheapest schedule that still zeroes the goal-gone failures.
prediction: Trim-only triggering already removes most goal-gone failures; adding a 10-step timer gives no extra pass but adds 5 to 10 percent tokens; the 95k trim target changes nothing for the goal because the first trim removes the oldest message either way.
test: 12-task screen, three arms of trim-only, timer 10, timer 30, each 36 runs, with trim target held at 80k; sweep range for the target is 80k to 95k only if the trim-only arm shows goal-gone failures. Refuted if the timer arms beat trim-only by 3 or more points, which would mean drift sets in before th

idea: Pin into the system prompt, trim-exempt
mechanism: The task text moves from the first user message into the system prompt at assembly time, so the oldest-first trim can never remove it. Targets lost the goal (11 of 40 failures, 9 with task text already trimmed) [F3, F4, F9].
prediction: Lost-the-goal count on the 20-run failure sample falls from about 5 to 1 or 2. Long-task pass rises 6 to 9 points, pass^3 rises more because trim timing is a seed-dependent source of flips [F1, F2]. Marginal token cost under 3 percent, since the text was already in the window before step 25.
test: Screen on 12 long tasks, seeds 1 to 3, 36 runs, with the task-text-in-context flag logged at every step. Refuted if the flag is always true yet lost-the-goal failures stay above 3 of 10 read failures, which would mean those runs drift for another reason.

idea: Trim bulky tool results before old messages
mechanism: When the window passes 100k, the harness first replaces the largest tool outputs older than 10 steps with a two-line stub naming the file and line range, and only then drops whole messages. Keeps the goal and the agent's own reasoning longer, and attacks stale context, since every stale-context run had a 300-plus-line file read in full [F6, F21].
prediction: Trim events per long run fall by at least half. Stale context and lost the goal both fall, unlike the summariser which traded one for the other [F14]. Tokens per run fall 5 to 10 percent because stubs are re-sent instead of full files.
test: 12-task screen, 36 runs, logging trim events and failure kinds. Refuted if stale-context failures rise, which would mean the agent needs the full file in view and re-reads do not happen.

idea: Trim thresholds as a sweep, with the goal pinned
mechanism: Today trimming starts at 100k and stops at 80k [F9]. With the goal pinned, the high mark and the low mark become free constants. A lower high mark trims earlier and oftener, and a wider gap trims more per event. The sweep tells how much history after the goal actually matters.
prediction: Pass rate is flat between 60k and 100k high marks once the goal is pinned, and tokens per run fall roughly in proportion to the high mark. If pass falls below the 100k setting at 60k, history matters and the gain is not from the pin alone.
test: Pin plus three settings: high 100k low 80k, high 80k low 60k, high 60k low 40k. 12 tasks, seeds 1 to 3, 108 runs. Refuted as a cost saver if the 60k setting loses 4 or more points against 100k.

idea: Goal-recall probe at fixed steps
mechanism: At steps 20, 30 and 40 the harness appends a system message asking for a one-line statement of the current goal, logs the answer, and scores it against the pinned text by a cheap string match or a second blind read. This turns "lost the goal" from a post-hoc label into a per-step measurement, so pinning variants can be compared on recall, not only on pass rate [F8, F17].
prediction: In the unpinned baseline, recall at step 40 falls under 50 percent and runs that fail recall at step 30 fail the task at twice the rate of runs that pass it. With the pin, recall stays above 90 percent at all three probes.
test: Run the probe on the 12-task screen in both baseline and pinned arms, 72 runs. Refuted if recall is high in the baseline, which would mean the agent still knows the goal and drifts for another reason, and the pin should be dropped from the ranked list.

idea: Goal plus recent window (trim threshold pushed to its floor)
mechanism: Limit case of the threshold sweep. The window holds only the pinned goal, the system prompt, and the last 20k tokens of history, trimmed at every step. What breaks first is stale context and loops, because the agent forgets what it already tried and read, and the fact that would show it is a rise in repeated cycles and stale-context labels [F5, F6]. The fix the limit suggests is a fixed, small window with the goal always at the head and recent steps always at the tail, which places the two things the model reads best [F22] and removes the middle entirely.
prediction: Tokens per run fall 40 percent or more. Lost the goal goes to near zero. Pass rate either holds within 4 points of the pinned 100k arm, which would make this the cheapest change on the list, or drops more than 6 points with repeated cycles up, which kills it.
test: 12 tasks, seeds 1 to 3, 36 runs, against the pinned 100k arm. Refuted if long-task pass is 6 or more points below the pinned arm or repeated cycles per run double.
breaks: Trimming is an emergency that should happen as late and as rarely as possible.
keeps: Same model, tools, step cap, pinned goal in the system prompt, same 48 tasks and seeds.
kill: Long-task pass more than 6 points below the pinned 100k arm on the screen, or median tokens per run not at least 30 percent lower.

idea: Goal echo as the newest message (re-injection pushed to every turn)
mechanism: Limit case of re-injection. The full task text is appended as the last message before every model call, in addition to the head pin. What breaks first is cost and habituation. Cost: a 500-token echo times 50 calls adds about 25k prompt tokens per run, over the 20 percent cap [F18]. Habituation: a message that never changes stops being read, which shows as unchanged lost-the-goal counts despite the echo. The fix the limit suggests is echo only at events: after each trim and once at step 25, where passing and failing runs diverge [F8]. The brief's third assumption, that pinning alone suffices, i
prediction: Event echo adds under 5 percent tokens. If head-only pinning leaves 3 or more lost-the-goal failures per 10 read failures and event echo cuts that to 1, placement matters and the assumption is wrong. If both arms are equal, head-only is enough and echo is dropped.
test: Three arms on 12 tasks, seeds 1 to 3: head pin only, head pin plus every-turn echo, head pin plus event echo, 108 runs. Refuted if event echo is within 2 points of head-only on pass and equal on lost-the-goal count.
source: https://agentic-ai.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ContextEngineering/manus/ and https://arxiv.org/html/2402.10962v4 for the drift motivation; the event trigger is own
breaks: The goal appears exactly once in the context.
keeps: Same pin at the head, same trim routine, same tools and cap.
kill: Event echo not at least 3 points above head-only on the screen, with lost-the-goal counts equal.

idea: Pin a pointer, not the text (pin length pushed to zero)
mechanism: Limit case of pin length. The pinned region shrinks to one line: "Your task is in TASK.md in the repository root; re-read it whenever unsure." The harness writes that file before the run. What breaks first is that the agent never reads it, which shows as the read_file log containing no TASK.md call after step 20 while lost-the-goal counts stay at baseline. The fix the limit suggests is the diagnostic itself: whether the model can be relied on to seek its goal separates a harness-fixable failure from a model limit.
prediction: If the model re-reads TASK.md in most runs after a trim, lost the goal falls as much as with the full pin and the pointer costs almost nothing. If re-reads are rare, "lost the goal" has a model-side part that no passive pin fixes, and that belongs in the model-limits section of the ranked list.
test: 12 tasks, seeds 1 to 3, 36 runs, logging reads of TASK.md by step. Refuted as a fix if fewer than half of runs re-read after step 25 and lost-the-goal stays at 2 or more per 10 read failures.
breaks: The goal must be present in the context window to be held.
keeps: Same tools, no new tool, same trim routine, same step cap and seeds.
kill: Pass rate 3 or more points below the full-text pin on the screen.

idea: Fire before the first trim, not after it
mechanism: Set N so the first copy lands before the window crosses 100k tokens, which by [F8] and [F9] is around step 25; a reminder that first fires at step 30 arrives after the agent has already lost the goal for several steps. First fire at step 10, then every 10, caps copies at 6 per 60-step run.
prediction: Lost-the-goal share of failures falls from 11 of 40 toward 4 or 5 of 40 on the 20-run sample, long-task pass moves from 31 to the 37 to 40 range, tokens per run rise under 8 percent for a task text of about 500 tokens.
test: Three arms on the 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3: first fire at 10, 20, 30 with the same every-10 cadence afterwards. Refuted if the step-10 arm does not beat the step-30 arm on lost-the-goal count in the failure-kind read. Sweep range worth running: N in {8, 12, 20}.
source: own, grounded in https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vstorm-co/pydantic-deepagents@main/docs/advanced/periodic-reminder.md which fires at turn 5 then every 10

idea: Full-text periodic reminder with no truncation
mechanism: Port the pydantic-deepagents periodic first-message reminder but drop its 400-character cut, because [F14] shows that shortened task text is the exact failure the summariser introduced. The wrapper is one sentence ("Your task, repeated verbatim:") plus the whole task message, nothing else.
prediction: Recovers roughly half of the 9 trimmed lost-the-goal runs in [F4], which is about 8 points of long-task pass; cost rises 5 to 8 percent, well under the 20 percent cap in [F18]; short tasks never reach step 10 trim so they are unaffected.
test: Screen on 12 tasks, then full 144 runs. Refuted if long-task pass gain is under 6 points or if the 20-run failure read shows lost-the-goal unchanged while the task text was verifiably in the window.

idea: Reminder re-enables the 20-step summariser
mechanism: The summariser helped stale context but hurt lost-the-goal because it dropped the task [F14]; with a verbatim reminder outside the summary, the drop becomes harmless. Run the pair as one arm to answer the open question on which changes combine.
prediction: The pair beats the reminder alone by 2 to 4 points through stale-context recovery, with cost rise still under 15 percent, since summaries shrink the window the reminder is added to.
test: Three arms on the 12-task screen: reminder alone, summariser alone, both. Refuted if the pair does not beat reminder alone on pass rate and stale-context count, or if lost-the-goal rises in the pair relative to reminder alone.

idea: Drift diagnostic that separates trimmed from untrimmed goal loss
mechanism: Two of the 11 lost-the-goal runs still had the task in the window [F4], so a reminder cannot help them; log per step whether the task text is live and whether the agent's last message names any task noun, so the failure read can split "trimmed" from "drifted anyway". This gives the model-limits section a count instead of a guess.
prediction: After the reminder, remaining lost-the-goal runs are mostly of the untrimmed kind, at a rate near 2 of 40, and that residue is labelled a model limit with evidence.
test: Add the two log columns to every run in the reminder arm, no extra runs. Refuted if untrimmed drift grows after the reminder, which would mean the reminder itself is disturbing the plan.

idea: Start-position reminder with eviction of old copies
mechanism: Removal 1 plus its reinvestment: instead of appending at the recent end, insert the verbatim task right after the system prompt every N steps and delete any earlier reminder copy. Lost in the Middle [F22] says the start is also a high-attention position, and a start copy stays at the start, while an end copy slides into the middle after ten tool results. One live copy keeps cost flat at one task-text worth.
prediction: Equal or better lost-the-goal recovery than the end-position arm at about one third of its token cost, since copies no longer accumulate. If the trimmer eats the start copy at each trim, the gap between reminders shows a goal-free window and this arm loses.
test: Two arms on the 12-task screen, end-position accumulating versus start-position single copy, same N. Refuted if start-position has more lost-the-goal failures in the 20-run read or lower pass rate by more than the 4-point seed spread.
breaks: A goal copy placed at the recent end of the context is better attended than one placed right after the system prompt.
keeps: Verbatim text, every-N trigger, same tools, same step cap, same trimmer rule otherwise.
kill: Panel average under 5 of 10 on keep rule, or start-position pass more than 4 points below end-position on the screen.

idea: Trim notice inside the reminder
mechanism: Removal 3 plus its reinvestment: the reminder opens with one sentence of harness truth, "Messages before step k were removed from your window, including the original task," then the verbatim task. The agent today cannot tell that it has forgotten anything [F4]; an explicit notice should make it re-check its plan against the goal rather than treat the copy as redundant repetition, which the Meta advisor result warns can be ignored or trigger needless work.
prediction: Among reminder arms, the notice variant has fewer lost-the-goal and fewer "plan continued as if nothing happened" turns in the step after the reminder; cost adds under 30 tokens per copy.
test: Two arms on the 12-task screen: bare verbatim reminder versus notice plus verbatim. Refuted if the notice arm shows no drop in lost-the-goal and the step-after-reminder messages do not mention the task more often.
breaks: The harness should stay silent about having trimmed the window.
keeps: Verbatim text, every-N trigger, end placement, no change to tools or trimming.
kill: Panel average under 5 of 10 on failure link, or lost-the-goal count equal to the bare-reminder arm on the 20-run read.

idea: Stop-time requirement map
mechanism: Removal 2 plus its reinvestment: the reminder stays inert during the run, but when the agent tries to stop the harness injects the verbatim task once more and requires a reply that pairs each task sentence with the file edit or command output that satisfies it, before the stop is accepted. This spends one extra model turn per run instead of six passive copies and targets lost-the-goal and the self-accepted wrong verifications in [F7], without the harness touching hidden tests [C8].
prediction: Lost-the-goal and wrong-verification together fall from 17 of 40 toward 10 of 40; runs that would have passed anyway spend about 2k extra tokens; a minority of runs resume work after the map and either pass or hit the step cap.
test: Two arms on the 12-task screen: periodic reminder alone versus periodic plus stop-time map. Refuted if the map arm does not beat the reminder-alone arm by at least 3 points or if its cost rise exceeds 15 percent.
breaks: The reminder is inert and the agent's stop is accepted without reference to the task text.
keeps: Verbatim text, every-N cadence during the run, no harness-run tests, same step cap counting the map turn as one step.
kill: Panel average under 5 of 10 on keep rule, or wrong-verification count unchanged in the 20-run read while cost rises more than 15 percent.

idea: Verbatim TASK slot with a deterministic string gate
mechanism: The summariser prompt becomes a fixed template whose first section is "TASK (copy verbatim)"; the harness string-matches that section against the original task text and rejects the summary on any mismatch, re-prompting with the mismatch quoted. This turns the 6-of-10 drop rate [F14] from a prompt-adherence problem into a zero-token mechanical check, which the brief's "prompt instructions are largely ignored" finding says is needed.
prediction: Lost-the-goal falls from 11/40 of failures to at most 4/40 on the failure sample, the stale-context gain of the tried summariser [F14] is kept, so long-task pass rises 8 to 11 points to about 39 to 42 percent. Tokens per run within plus or minus 10 percent of 65k, since rejections cost one extra sum
test: 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3, 36 runs, logging per compaction whether the gate fired and the task-text-in-context flag at every step. Refuted if the gate rejects under 5 percent of summaries (then it adds nothing over the plain summariser) or if lost-the-goal share on the screen's failures does not

idea: keep_first plus end re-injection (control arm)
mechanism: The system prompt and task text are excluded from the summarised span and the task text is appended verbatim as the newest message after each compaction, so it sits at both ends of the window [F22]. This breaks assumption 2 on purpose: it is the one-line fix the panel will ask about, and every other sketch here is only worth keeping if it beats this arm or combines with it.
prediction: 9 of 11 lost-the-goal runs had no task text in context [F4]; if trimming is the cause in most, long pass rises 8 to 12 points. If the gain is under 4 points, those runs drift for another reason, which answers the open question and redirects effort to the behavioural sketches below. Cost about 300 ex
test: Same 36-run screen as sketch 1, run as a paired arm, same seeds. Refuted for its own sake if long pass gain is under 4 points with the task text present in every step. Refuted as a control if sketch 1 matches it within 2 points, in which case assumption 2 can be kept.
target: model limits (separates trimming-caused loss from drift), keep rule

idea: Token-triggered compaction instead of every 20 steps
mechanism: The summariser fires when the window passes a token threshold and compacts down to a target, keeping the last few messages verbatim, rather than on a step count. A 20-step span with full reads of 300-line files [F6] can pass 100k before step 20, so the oldest-first trimmer [F9] fires first and removes the task text before the summariser ever runs; in short-output runs the summariser fires needlessly and discards detail.
prediction: Runs in which the raw trimmer ever fires fall from most long runs to near zero, so the summariser rather than the trimmer decides what survives. Alone it should add 2 to 4 points; combined with sketch 1 it should add 1 to 3 points on top and cut tokens 5 to 15 percent.
test: Sweep trigger 60k, 75k, 90k; target 30k, 40k, 50k; keep-last 4, 8 messages on the 12-task screen, one seed per cell for the screen (9 cells, 108 runs), then seeds 1 to 3 on the best cell. Refuted if no cell reduces trimmer firings below 20 percent of runs without raising tokens over 20 percent.

idea: Requirement ledger reconciled across summaries
mechanism: At step 0 one model call turns the task text into a numbered acceptance checklist of 3 to 8 items. Each summary must contain a table with every item id, a status of done, open or blocked, and the command and output line that is the evidence; the harness rejects any summary missing an id or marking an item done without a quoted command. This targets wrong verification [F7] as well as lost the goal, because a summary can no longer declare success without a cited check.
prediction: Lost-the-goal and wrong-verification together fall from 17/40 to at most 8/40 on the failure sample; long pass rises 6 to 9 points. Extra cost about 800 tokens at step 0 plus about 400 per compaction, under 5 percent.
test: 36-run screen with the ledger logged per compaction. Refuted if more than 20 percent of items marked done lack a real passing command in the trajectory (the gate is gamed), or if the combined share of the two failure kinds does not fall.
source: builds on https://factory.com/news/evaluating-compression; the reconciliation gate is own

idea: Readback gate after compaction (import from air traffic control)
mechanism: Shared structure: a short instruction is issued once over a lossy channel to an actor who acts on it much later, so the protocol makes the actor read it back and the issuer correct it before action. Instantiation: after each compaction, and once at step 25 [F8], the harness withholds tool calls until the agent quotes the goal and lists the checks it will run; the harness scores overlap with the original text, and on a miss replies with the original as a correction. Correspondence breaks where the readback itself re-injects the goal, so the check and the reminder are confounded, and where the a
prediction: Readback misses occur in at least 30 percent of post-compaction points under today's summariser and near 0 percent with sketch 1. Lost-the-goal falls to 3/40 or fewer, long pass up 6 to 9 points, about 400 tokens per readback, under 3 percent cost.
test: 36-run screen with a paired arm that injects the goal without asking for a readback. Refuted if the readback arm does not beat the inject-only arm by at least 2 points, meaning the check adds nothing the reminder did not.
breaks: Goal preservation is judged by whether the text is in the window; this judges it by whether the agent can reproduce it and blocks action until it can.
keeps: Model-produced summaries at the same interval, same four tools, step cap 60, hidden tests untouched.
kill: Readback passes at 95 percent or more yet lost-the-goal share on the failure sample is unchanged, which shows the failures are drift, not amnesia.

idea: Drift-triggered goal re-injection (import from concept drift detection)
mechanism: Shared structure: in streaming learning a cheap statistic on recent inputs is monitored against a control limit, and the system re-anchors when it crosses, so the trigger is behavioural rather than scheduled. Instantiation: the harness extracts identifiers and paths from the task text and the first 10 steps [F8], keeps a running overlap score with the last 5 tool calls, and when a cumulative-sum statistic crosses a limit it injects the task text plus "state how your last three actions serve it" with no model call for detection. Correspondence breaks when legitimate exploration of a dependency
prediction: The statistic fires before failure in at least 7 of 11 lost-the-goal runs replayed offline, including the 2 that still had the task text, and in under 15 percent of passing runs. Live, long pass up 5 to 8 points on top of sketch 1, cost under 2 percent.
test: First replay the 40 read failures and 20 passing runs offline against the statistic, zero new runs. Then a 36-run screen. Refuted offline if it fires before failure in fewer than half the lost-the-goal runs or in more than 30 percent of passing runs' steps.
target: model limits (answers whether the 2 of 11 drift for another reason), failure link
breaks: The moment to protect the goal is compaction; this re-injects when behaviour departs from the goal, whether or not the text is still in the window.
keeps: The summariser, its interval and prompt, trimming thresholds, and the retry.
kill: Offline replay shows the statistic separates failing and passing runs no better than a coin, or live false alarms raise tokens over 20 percent.

idea: Decode-tested summaries (import from lossy compression)
mechanism: Shared structure: an encoding is judged by decoding it and comparing to the source on the dimensions that matter, not by trusting the encoder. Instantiation: after the summariser writes a candidate, a cold model call with only the system prompt and that candidate answers three fixed probes, the task, the required checks, and the files changed so far; the harness scores the first two by overlap with the task text and the third exactly against its own log of edit_file paths, rejects on failure with the probe appended, and after two failures keeps raw messages for that cycle. This also measures s
prediction: Summary quality is not uniform: rejection rates differ by task by more than 30 points. Stale context and lost the goal both fall, with long pass up 7 to 10 points, about 1.5k tokens per compaction, under 8 percent cost.
test: 36-run screen logging rejection rate and probe scores per compaction. Refuted if rejections are under 5 percent (identical to sketch 1) or over 50 percent (compaction stalls and cost exceeds 20 percent), or if it does not beat sketch 1 by at least 2 points on the full 144 runs.
source: own; related to the open judge-verified compaction item at https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2605.23296.md, but uses harness-known ground truth instead of a judge
breaks: A summary is accepted as produced; this accepts it only after a decode test against facts the harness knows.
keeps: Model summariser, task text inside the summarised span, same interval, same tools and step cap.
kill: Probe scores show no relation to run outcome on the 20-run failure sample, so the gate measures nothing that matters.

idea: Fingerprinted re-run detector with a factual nudge
mechanism: The harness hashes each run_shell call with its output; when the same (command, output hash) pair appears twice in the last six calls with an edit in between, it injects one message stating the observation ("pytest run 3 times, identical 4 failures, 2 edits to parser.py, no change") and the rule "state what you expect the next edit to change before you run again." Loops are 9 of 40 failures [F5] and burn 2,400 tokens per cycle until the cap [F5, F12], so interrupting at the second repeat cuts both the failure and its cost; the factual form avoids the LangChain finding that a bare "reconsider"
prediction: Loop failures in the 20-run sample fall from about 9 of 40 to 3 or 4 of 40; long-task pass rises 4 to 7 points; tokens per run fall 5 to 10 percent because capped loop runs are the most expensive runs. Some former loops convert to "gave up early" rather than passes.
test: Screen on the 12 long tasks whose failed runs were labeled loop, seeds 1 to 3 (36 runs). Refuted if loop-labeled failures do not drop by at least half or if pass on those 12 does not rise by 2 or more tasks across seeds. Then full 48 by 3 seeds (144 runs) against the keep rule [F18].

idea: Threshold and fingerprint-key sweep
mechanism: Two constants decide false positives and lateness: how many repeats trigger (2 or 3) and what is hashed (command only, command plus output, or command plus output plus last edited file, seed 12). Command-only flags legitimate read-after-write re-runs, which the LangChain forum thread reports as the main false-positive source; adding the output hash makes a changed failure count read as progress, and hashing within a six-call window catches A-B-A-B alternation for free, so the "exact repeats" assumption need not be leaned on even though this part keeps it.
prediction: Repeat threshold 2 with (command, output) key gives the best trade: it triggers about 2,400 tokens earlier per loop than threshold 3 [F5] and fires on under 5 percent of runs that go on to pass. Command-only key fires on 20 percent or more of passing runs and hurts short tasks.
test: Log fingerprints passively on the existing 144-run baseline logs (zero new runs): count how many passing runs would have triggered under each of the six settings. Refuted as a useful knob if all six settings fire on fewer than 3 percent of passing runs (then threshold does not matter) or if none kee

idea: Step-25 checkpoint independent of repetition
mechanism: Passing and failing runs are indistinguishable for 10 steps and diverge after step 25 [F8], so a detector that waits for a repeat fires late. At tool call 25 the harness injects a fixed three-field prompt: what is confirmed, what is unknown, what the next test should show. This is a Reflexion-style written reflection moved mid-run [F20], costing about 400 tokens once, and it gives the loop detector a stated expectation to grade later.
prediction: Among runs that would have looped, a third never start the cycle because the expectation is written before the first re-run; long-task pass rises 2 to 4 points on its own and the effect adds to the detector rather than overlapping, since it fires at a different time. Cost rises under 1 percent.
test: 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3, with and without the checkpoint, detector off (36 plus the existing baseline). Refuted if loop-labeled failures are unchanged or if runs that passed at baseline start failing after the checkpoint on 2 or more tasks.
source: builds on Reflexion [F20] and the step-25 observation [F8]; own placement

idea: Prune the cycle instead of commenting on it
mechanism: Subtract the post-loop message. What it buys per the facts is little: the model already sees the repeats and ignores them, and each message adds tokens at exactly the point where the window is filling. Reinvest in context surgery: on detection the harness deletes all but the first and last instance of the cycle from the context and replaces them with a one-line ledger ("cycles 2 to 5 removed: same edit, same output"). Loops at 2,400 tokens per cycle [F5] are what pushes runs over the 100k trim line that drops the task text [F4, F9], so removing the cycle protects the goal text and frees room t
prediction: In loop runs the task text stays in context to the end (today it is gone in most long failures [F4]); loop failures fall to about 4 of 40, and lost-the-goal failures co-occurring with loops fall too. Tokens per run fall 10 percent or more. Pass up 4 to 6 points.
test: On the 12 loop-prone tasks, seeds 1 to 3, compare pruning against the factual nudge (72 runs). Refuted if the pruned arm does not keep the task text in context in at least 80 percent of runs that trigger, or if its pass rate is lower than the nudge arm.
source: own; the pi-deadloop tool prunes but also nudges, this removes the nudge entirely: https://pi.dev/packages/pi-deadloop?page=23
target: keep rule (cost) and failure link (loop plus lost the goal)
breaks: The intervention after a detected loop is a message to the agent; here it is a change to the agent's context with no message.
keeps: The same fingerprint detector, the same trigger, the same step cap, retries untouched; measured with the same seeds and failure labels.
kill: Pass on the 12-task screen below the factual-nudge arm, or task text present in under 80 percent of triggered runs.

idea: Revert the tree and hand back the tried list
mechanism: Subtract the agent's accumulated loop edits. The facts say they buy nothing: the test output is identical after every one of them [F5]. Reinvest in a clean state: on detection the harness snapshots had been taken before the first cycle; it reverts the working tree to that snapshot and injects the combined diff of every attempt under "tried, test output unchanged." The agent then faces the original failing test with a written list of what does not work, instead of a tree carrying several half-applied patches that can themselves cause the unchanged output.
prediction: Loop runs that pass after intervention rise from near zero today to 30 to 50 percent of detected loops, worth 4 to 7 points of long-task pass. Runs where the loop edits were partly right lose that progress and show up as new "gave up early" failures; the net is positive only if those are under a thi
test: 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3, revert-plus-tried-list against the factual nudge (72 runs); hand-label the 20-run sample for "progress lost on revert." Refuted if more than a third of triggered runs lose a partial fix, or if pass is not above the nudge arm.
target: failure link (loop converted to pass) and model limits (shows which loops the model cannot escape even from a clean state)
breaks: The harness never changes the repository state the agent built; here it rolls the tree back to before the loop.
keeps: Same detector and trigger, hidden tests untouched [C8], step cap and retry policy unchanged, same 144-run measurement.
kill: Partial progress lost in over a third of triggered runs, or long-task pass on the screen at or below the nudge arm.

idea: Graded predictions as the loop signal
mechanism: Subtract the system-prompt re-run rule, which costs attention in a 900-token prompt [F9] and is not enforced [F10]. Reinvest in the tool schema: run_shell takes an optional `expect` string, and on any command that matches a prior fingerprint the field becomes required, so a bare re-run is rejected by the tool. After the run the harness scores the expectation against the output (did the named test or line change) and keeps a running count shown in the tool result ("2 of 2 predictions wrong"). Three wrong predictions in a row is the loop trigger, replacing "same output twice." This answers the o
prediction: Loop failures fall to 3 of 40 or fewer; wrong-verification failures also fall because the expectation forces a concrete pass condition before each run [F7]. Tool-refusal events add under 300 tokens per run. Pass up 5 to 8 points; cost flat or down.
test: 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3, schema-enforced prediction against prompt-rule prediction (72 runs). Refuted if the agent fills `expect` with boilerplate in over half of re-runs (hand-read 20 runs), or if loop failures do not fall below the prompt-rule arm.
source: own; the untried item "prediction before re-running a test" [F15] moved from prompt into tool contract
breaks: The loop signal is an unchanged tool output; here it is the agent's stated expectation being wrong, enforced by the tool rather than the prompt.
keeps: Same four tools, same step cap, the same fingerprint hashing, retries untouched, same measurement plan.
kill: Boilerplate expectations in over half of re-runs, or loop failures not below the prompt-rule arm on the screen.

idea: Rule-versus-prediction factorial screen
mechanism: The open question asks whether a loop is better broken by a rule or by a prediction, and the budget allows about 15 full measurements [F19], so the two must not each spend one. A 2x2 screen on the 12 loop-prone tasks crosses detector (on or off) with prediction (prompt rule or none), 4 arms by 36 runs, and only the winning cell goes to the full 48. This fits the ordering the measurement plan demands and gives the panel a tested answer to a listed open question instead of an opinion.
prediction: The detector alone gives most of the gain and prediction alone gives little, because the facts say the agent never states expectations unprompted [F5], not that it cannot act on them; the combination is additive, not cancelling. If the two cancel, that itself rules out the stacked-intervention risk
test: 144 screening runs, then one full measurement of 144 runs: 288 runs total, about 12 percent of budget. Refuted as a plan if no arm beats baseline on the 12 tasks by 2 tasks or more across seeds, in which case loop breaking drops in the ranked list.

idea: Offline replay before any run
mechanism: Run the proposed (tool, args, output) hash detector over the existing logs of the 40 read failed runs and an equal set of passing long runs, with thresholds 2 and 3, and count where it would have fired. This costs zero suite runs and settles the false-positive question before a single measurement is spent, since [F8] says passing and failing runs look alike before step 25.
prediction: At threshold 2 the detector fires in all 9 loop runs by step 30 and in at least 15 percent of passing runs, mostly on legitimate test re-runs after edits that did not change output. At threshold 3 passing-run firing falls under 5 percent with loop recall at 8 of 9.
test: Replay over real logs only, never the synthetic CSV [C9]. If threshold 3 fires in more than 10 percent of passing runs, the rule is too blunt for the keep rule and the idea is dead before screening.

idea: Threshold and scope sweep on run_shell only
mechanism: Restrict the hash key to run_shell calls whose command matches a test or build pattern, and sweep the firing threshold over 2 and 3 identical results. Edit and read tools are excluded because the loop in [F5] is edit-then-test, and the signal lives in the unchanged test output, which answers the OpenHands polling complaint by never watching polling-style reads.
prediction: Loop failures in the 20-run failure sample fall from 9 of 40 to about 4 of 40 at threshold 2. Long-task pass rises 3 to 5 points. Tokens per run fall about 8 percent because 9 loop runs stop burning 2,400 tokens per cycle to the cap [F5, F12].
test: 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3, two arms (threshold 2, threshold 3) against baseline, 108 runs. Refuted if loop-kind failures do not fall by half or if short-task pass drops at all.

idea: Interrupt message that demands a prediction and shows the diff
mechanism: When the detector fires, the message is not generic. It quotes the identical output, shows the diff of the agent's last two edits, and requires a one-line answer to "what will your next edit change in this output" before run_shell is re-enabled. This targets [F5] directly: the agent never stated what it expected, and [F15] lists prediction-before-rerun as untried.
prediction: Among runs where the detector fires, the share that changes strategy within three steps rises from near zero to above half. Loop failures convert to passes in about a third of cases, worth roughly 4 to 5 points on long tasks, with the remainder becoming gave-up-early or still loops.
test: Same 12-task screen as the threshold sweep, adding a third arm with the rich message at the better threshold. Refuted if the rich message converts no more loop runs to passes than the plain stop-and-rethink message, which would support SWE-smith's view that repetition is a symptom of task difficulty
source: own, building on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.21798 (warning on repetition)

idea: Cached output instead of a re-run
mechanism: Push the threshold to its limit of one. A repeated identical run_shell call with no intervening edit_file is not executed. The harness returns a two-line result: the previous output hash, and "no file changed since this command last ran." What breaks first is a legitimate re-run after an environment step such as an install. The fact that would show it is a short-task pass drop [F18]. The fix is the gate: the cache is bypassed when any tool call other than read_file or search occurred since the last identical run.
prediction: Each avoided cycle saves about 2,300 of the 2,400 tokens [F5]. Loop runs end their cycling within two interrupts instead of running to the cap, cutting tokens per run on long tasks by about 10 percent. Pass rises 3 to 6 points through the freed steps and the explicit staleness signal.
test: 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3, one arm, 36 runs plus baseline. Refuted if short-task pass on the screen falls by more than the seed spread, or if the agent responds to the cached result by rewording the command to escape the cache more than once per run.
breaks: The detector may only insert a message; it never substitutes a tool result.
keeps: Hash key of (tool, args, output), harness-side detection, the stop-and-rethink message on the second firing, unchanged step cap and trimming.
kill: A panel mean below 6 on keep rule, or any short-task pass drop in the screen.

idea: Collapse repeated cycles out of the context window
mechanism: Push the number of interrupts to its limit and ask what fills the window. Ten cycles at 2,400 tokens is 24k tokens, which pushes the context past the 100k trim point sooner and drops the oldest message first, the task text [F4, F9]. A loop therefore manufactures a lost-the-goal failure. The fix is that on each detected repeat, the harness deletes the earlier identical cycle from the window and keeps one copy with a counter. This treats the detector as a context-handling step and ties two failure kinds together.
prediction: Long runs that enter a loop stop triggering trimming. Task-text-in-context at the end of a run rises in the loop subset from a minority to nearly all. Combined loop and lost-the-goal failures fall by 5 or more of the 20 in the failure sample. Tokens per run fall about 12 percent.
test: 12-task screen with the detector alone versus detector plus collapse, 72 runs. Refuted if the collapse arm shows no reduction in trimming events among runs that fired, or if the agent, having lost sight of its own repeated attempts, repeats them again at a higher rate than the plain-detector arm.
breaks: Everything the agent did stays in the context until the trimmer removes it from the oldest end.
keeps: Hash-based detection, thresholds of 2 to 3, the interrupt message, no change to the model or to the hidden tests.
kill: A panel mean below 6 on failure link, or trimming events unchanged in the fired subset.

idea: End the run early and hand a reflection to the retry
mechanism: Push interrupt count to its limit: an agent that ignores two interrupts will ignore a third, and the run burns to the cap. Instead, on the second firing the harness ends the run, asks the model for a 150-token Reflexion-style note on what was tried and what the test kept saying, and prepends that note to the already-kept retry [F13, F20]. Loop runs are the ones most likely to need the retry anyway, so ending them at about step 30 cuts the first run's cost roughly in half and funds the retry within the 20 percent cost rule.
prediction: Pair cost on loop-detected tasks falls from about 130k tokens to about 95k. The pair pass rate rises from 44 percent to about 50 percent because the retry no longer re-enters the same loop. The retry's loop rate in the failure sample drops near zero.
test: 12-task screen, pairs on seeds 1 to 3, early-stop-with-note versus current retry from scratch, 72 runs. Refuted if the retry with the note enters the same cycle as often as the plain retry, or if early stops cut off runs that would have passed under the cap at a rate above the seed spread.
source: own, building on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.0 (none); Reflexion as cited in [F20]
breaks: A run continues until the step cap; only the agent's own stop ends it.
keeps: The detector and its hash key, the retry from scratch with a different seed, the hidden tests untouched, one retry at most.
kill: A panel mean below 6 on keep rule, or pair pass rate not above the 44 percent of the current retry.

idea: Honest ceiling for the loop fix
mechanism: State the model limit before the panel asks. Loops are 9 of 40 failures, about 15 percent of all long runs. SWE-smith found interrupting repetition cut repetition but left resolution unchanged, so the realistic conversion is a third, about 5 points. The detector therefore passes the keep rule only through its token saving combined with pinning or the retry, and the proposal should say so and rank it accordingly.
prediction: On the full 48-task measurement the detector alone lands at plus 3 to 5 points, under the 6-point keep line, but with tokens per run down about 10 percent. Paired with pinned task text it reaches the keep line because the saved tokens offset pinning's cost.
test: Full measurement of detector alone and detector plus pinning, 288 runs. Refuted in the useful direction if the detector alone clears 6 points, which would mean loops are more harness-fixable than SWE-smith suggests.

idea: Prediction with a refutation clause
mechanism: The system-prompt rule asks for two free-text lines before any repeated command: "I expect X to change because of edit Y" and "If I see Z instead, the hypothesis is wrong and I will not re-run again." The second line is what [F5] shows missing: loop runs re-ran without a stated expectation, so no result could count as evidence against the current approach.
prediction: Loop failures in the 20-run failure sample fall from about 9 of 40 to 5 or fewer; average cycles per loop run drop from "until cap" to under 4; long pass rises 4 to 7 points at a cost of about 60 tokens per re-run, well under the 20 percent cap in [F18].
test: 12-task screen, seeds 1 to 3, 36 runs, with a trajectory grep for the two lines. Refuted if fewer than 70 percent of repeated commands carry both lines, or if runs with the lines still cycle past 4 repeats as often as baseline.
source: builds on https://alphaxiv.org/abs/2304.02195 (hypothesis-then-experiment); the refutation line is own

idea: Harness echo after the re-run
mechanism: When the harness sees a repeated command it stores the preceding prediction and appends it under the tool result with one question: "Held, or not? One line." This closes the gap the brief flags, that agents notice surprises but do not act on them: the comparison is forced into the next turn instead of being hoped for.
prediction: The share of re-runs followed by a different edit, rather than another identical re-run, rises above 60 percent of loop-prone runs; loop failures fall by 3 or more of 9; cost is under 40 tokens per re-run.
test: Run the prediction rule with and without the echo on the 12-task screen, 72 runs. Refuted if the echo arm does not reduce identical consecutive re-runs by at least a third relative to the prediction-only arm.

idea: Trigger threshold for the prediction rule
mechanism: Ask for a prediction only from the second identical (tool, args) hash onward, not on every test run. Passing runs also re-run tests, so a rule firing every time taxes the 31 percent that pass today; a hash gate confines the tax to runs that already show the [F5] pattern.
prediction: Token cost of the rule falls from roughly 3 percent of a 65k run to under 1 percent with no loss of loop-breaking effect; pass gain unchanged within the 4-point seed spread of [F18].
test: Sweep the threshold over 1, 2 and 3 identical hashes on the 12-task screen, 108 runs. Refuted if threshold 2 or 3 loses more than 2 points of pass against threshold 1, or if threshold 1 costs under 1 percent anyway, which makes the gate pointless.

idea: Refuted hypotheses carried into the retry
mechanism: The retry from scratch in [F13] today learns nothing from the failed run. The harness collects the prediction lines whose results did not hold and prepends them to the retry as "already tried and refuted". The loop that killed run one cannot be re-entered in run two.
prediction: Pair pass rises from 44 percent by 3 to 6 points; cost rises by under 500 tokens per retry; failure kinds of the retry shift away from loop.
test: Compare retries with and without the refuted list on tasks that failed with loop kind in seed 1, 12 tasks, seeds 2 and 3. Refuted if retried runs loop on the same command hash at the same rate as plain retries.

idea: Zero-information re-run veto
mechanism: Rerepresented as a measurement: a test run is a measurement, and a re-run whose predicted output equals the last observed output has zero expected information. The prompt rule becomes: you may re-run a command only if your prediction names a line of output that will differ from last time; otherwise edit, read, or reread the task first. The prediction stops being an annotation and becomes a condition on the action.
prediction: Identical consecutive re-runs drop below 1 per run on average; loop failures fall from 9 to 3 or fewer of 40; long pass rises 5 to 8 points. Cost falls, since [F5] shows each avoided cycle saves about 2,400 tokens.
test: 12-task screen, 36 runs, counting consecutive identical command hashes and the presence of a "will differ" line. Refuted if the agent re-runs with a prediction that merely restates the previous output in more than 30 percent of repeats, which means the rule is obeyed in letter only.
breaks: The agent may re-run any command at any time and the prediction only describes it; here a re-run without a differing prediction is not permitted.
keeps: Free-text prediction, prompt rule without a harness gate, same four tools, step cap 60, same seeds and suite.
kill: Loop failures above 6 of 40 in the full 144-run measurement, or any short-task pass drop.

idea: Diff view on repeated commands
mechanism: Rerepresented as what is shown: on a repeated command the harness returns a diff of the output against the previous run of the same command, with the raw output only on first run. "0 lines changed" becomes a literal observation the agent cannot miss, and the 2,400-token cycle of [F5] shrinks to a few hundred tokens, which also slows the trimming that causes [F4].
prediction: Loop runs that see "0 lines changed" twice switch strategy in over half of cases; tokens per long run fall 10 to 20 percent; loop and lost-the-goal failures both fall.
test: 12-task screen, 36 runs, with the diff view and no other change. Refuted if agents ignore the diff and keep cycling at baseline rates, or if the diff hides a failure detail the agent needed and pass drops on tasks with changing test output.
source: own; SWE-agent's short tool outputs in [F21] are the nearest precedent
breaks: Each tool result is shown raw and in full regardless of history; here the second showing of a result is only its change.
keeps: Prediction rule as free text, trimming policy, step cap, tools and seeds unchanged.
kill: Long pass gain under 6 points, or pass drop above 2 points on tasks whose test output legitimately changes between runs.

idea: Harness states the null prediction
mechanism: Flipping who predicts: when a command repeats, the harness prefixes the tool result slot with "Last time this printed the following; unless your edits touched its path, expect the same," and asks the agent to state in one line what will differ. The agent is no longer asked to invent a prediction from nothing; it must argue against a stated default, which is a cheaper and more reliable form of the SAMULE comparison.
prediction: The rate of runs where the agent states a specific differing line rises above the free-prompt rule by 20 points; loop failures fall by 4 or more of 9; cost under 100 tokens per repeat.
test: Three arms on the 12-task screen, 108 runs: no rule, agent-only prediction, harness null prediction. Refuted if the null-prediction arm does not beat the agent-only arm on identical consecutive re-runs.
source: own; departs from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.20562 where the agent alone forecasts
breaks: The agent is the one who predicts; here the harness supplies the default prediction and the agent only states the deviation.
keeps: Free-text answer, no hard gate, same tools and step cap, same measurement plan.
kill: Null-prediction arm within the 4-point seed spread of the agent-only arm on the full 48-task measurement.

idea: Pinned task block re-injected after every compaction
mechanism: Drops the assumption that a well-timed summariser keeps the task. The harness stores the task text and constraints in a separate buffer and re-inserts them verbatim as the first message after every trim or summary, so neither mechanism can remove them.
prediction: task_text_in_context_at_end becomes 100 percent on real logs; lost-the-goal failures fall to near zero; cost rises by under 100 tokens per compaction.
test: 12-task screen, 3 seeds, pinned versus unpinned with the existing every-20-steps summariser. Refuted if lost-the-goal count does not fall or long pass does not rise.

idea: Keep-first-2 plus keep-last with mechanical target
mechanism: Adds keep-first to the token-triggered summariser: system prompt and task message are never sent to the summariser, and the target size is met by choosing how many middle messages to summarise, not by asking the summariser for a length.
prediction: Trimmer firings near zero and task text present at end on every run, with tokens flat; stale-context count unchanged.
test: One cell of the sweep (75k, 40k, keep-last 8) run with and without keep-first-2, 12 tasks, 2 seeds. Refuted if task-text presence is equal in both arms.

idea: Mask only tool outputs over a size cut, never summarise
mechanism: Replace tool outputs older than K steps and larger than S tokens with a one-line placeholder naming the file and line range. The task text, agent actions and reasoning are never touched, so no summariser exists to drop the goal.
prediction: Tokens per long task down 20 to 40 percent; lost-the-goal failures at the raw-agent level or lower; the agent re-reads a masked file when needed, which also reduces stale-context failures.
test: 12-task screen, 3 seeds, masking versus the every-20-steps summariser. Refuted if long pass is lower than the summariser arm or tokens are not lower.
breaks: The rule that compaction is an LLM-written summary.
kill: Long-task pass more than 2 points below the summariser arm on 3 seeds, or stale-context failures up by more than 2 cases.

idea: Pin the agent's current plan and done-list the same way as the task
mechanism: For the part about a scratch notes file, the harness holds a short structured block (goal, plan, done, next) that the agent updates by a tool call, and re-injects it after every compaction alongside the task, so plan state survives compaction without passing through the summariser.
prediction: Loop failures fall, since the done-list shows repeated cycles; lost-the-goal stays at zero; added cost under 300 tokens per compaction.
test: 12-task screen, 2 seeds, pinned task only versus pinned task plus plan block. Refuted if loop count and pass are unchanged.
part: scratch notes file with plan and done-list

idea: Judge-checked summary with a task-survival gate
mechanism: After the summariser writes a summary, a cheap check asks whether the verbatim task text and each listed constraint are present; if not, the harness appends them and logs the miss. Combines token-triggered compaction with judge-verified compaction.
prediction: The miss log directly measures how often the summariser drops the task, replacing luka's 6-of-10 hand count; task presence at end reaches 100 percent; cost up under 5 percent.
test: 12-task screen, 1 seed, log misses. Refuted as a fix if pass does not rise; refuted as a measurement if the miss rate is zero while lost-the-goal failures persist.

idea: Agent-chosen compaction points at plan boundaries
mechanism: Instead of a token or step trigger, the agent is given a compact tool and the prompt tells it to call it when a sub-goal is finished, with the task pinned. Flips the rule that the harness decides when to compact.
prediction: Compactions fall in number and land at natural boundaries, so stale-context and lost-the-goal both drop; risk that the agent never calls it and the trimmer takes over.
test: 12-task screen, 2 seeds, with a hard token fallback. Refuted if the agent calls compact in under half of long runs or tokens rise over 20 percent.
breaks: The rule that compaction timing is a harness parameter, not an agent decision.
kill: Cost up more than 20 percent, or long-task pass gain under 2 points on 3 seeds.

idea: Pinned task field
mechanism: Drop the assumption that the copy is a message. Store the task text as a protected field the trimmer and summariser may never remove or rewrite, with no schedule and no eviction, so the task sits at the start permanently.
prediction: Lost-the-goal fails fall to the level of untrimmed runs, with zero added tokens and no cache breaks, and no change on short tasks.
test: 12-task screen, five seeds, pinned versus baseline; refuted if task text is present at the end of all pinned runs yet lost-the-goal count in the 20-run read does not fall by at least 3.
source: own, matching luka's untried item "keeping the task text pinned"

idea: Bookend copy
mechanism: Keep one protected copy at the start and one evicted-and-refreshed copy at the end, so the task occupies both high-attention ends of the U-shape at a cost of two copies.
prediction: Lost-the-goal count lower than either single-position arm, cost under plus 5 percent in dollars since the end copy is appended at the tail where the cache already breaks.
test: Three arms on the screen, start-only, end-only, bookend; refuted if bookend is not below both on lost-the-goal or exceeds plus 10 percent cost.

idea: Trim-triggered reinsertion only
mechanism: Reinsert the task text only on the first model call after a trim or summary removed it, as the first message after the trim boundary, never on a fixed schedule.
prediction: Same task-presence rate as the every-N arm with fewer prefix rewrites and lower dollar cost, no change on runs that never trim.
test: Count cache writes and dollars per task in both arms over the screen; refuted if the trim-triggered arm has more lost-the-goal fails than every-N by more than 2 of 20.

idea: Summary template with a verbatim task header
mechanism: In the context summarising part, force every summary to begin with the untouched task text copied by the harness, not written by the model, so the summariser can no longer shorten or drop it.
prediction: Luka's 6-of-10 dropped-task summaries fall to 0 of 10, and the summariser's stale-context gain survives without the lost-the-goal rise.
test: Rerun the 20-step summariser with the header on the screen; refuted if lost-the-goal fails still exceed the no-summariser baseline in the 20-run read.

idea: Reminder from the notes file
mechanism: Combine the reminder with the Manus recitation pattern: the agent keeps a notes file with goal, plan, and done items, and the harness injects that file, not the raw task, as the single evicted reminder every N steps.
prediction: Larger gain than a verbatim reminder on tasks over 40 steps because the reminder carries status, as in the memory-agent result, at a cost of one short file per reminder.
test: Two arms, verbatim versus notes-file reminder, same N; refuted if the notes arm is not above verbatim on pass by more than the seed spread or costs more than plus 15 percent.

idea: Task always last
mechanism: Flip the chronological rule: on every call the harness builds the prompt as system prompt, full history, then the task text as the final user message, so the task is always the most recent token span, with one copy and no accumulation.
prediction: Lost-the-goal fails near zero on trimmed and untrimmed runs, cost up one task-text worth per call, and a risk that the model answers the task afresh instead of continuing the last tool result.
test: Screen against end-with-eviction; refuted if loop fails rise by more than 3 of 20 in the read or pass falls below the end arm by more than the seed spread.
breaks: The context is a chronological transcript whose last message is the latest tool result
kill: Panel average under 5 of 10 on model limits, or loop fails up more than 3 of 20 in the blind read

idea: Replay as a cost lever, not a pass lever
mechanism: Drop the assumption that interruption changes outcomes. In the replay, for each loop failure compute steps and tokens after first fire; propose the rule as ending the run early and handing to the existing one-retry default, and predict the cost saving per loop failure.
prediction: Tokens after first fire in loop failures are a sizeable slice of those runs' cost, so pass stays level while long-task cost falls, which satisfies the cost half of the keep rule with no pass claim at risk.
test: If median tokens after first fire are under a tenth of the run's tokens, the saving is too small and the idea is dropped.

idea: Normalised near-duplicate replay
mechanism: Before hashing, strip timings, temp paths, PIDs and line numbers from outputs, and also compute a token-set similarity between the current output and the last output for the same (tool, args). Replay both exact and near-duplicate variants side by side.
prediction: Near-duplicate matching fires earlier in loop failures than exact hashing and raises recall, at the price of some extra fires in passing runs.
test: If near-duplicate first fire is not earlier than exact first fire in most loop failures, keep the exact hash.

idea: Test-rerun-only detector
mechanism: Apply the rule only to the test-run tool: fire when the test command is rerun and the normalised failing-test set is unchanged since the last run, ignoring all other tools.
prediction: Recall on loop failures stays close to the full rule because loops in coding agents centre on edit-then-test, while fires in passing runs fall sharply because file reads and polls are exempt.
test: Replay on the same logs; if the test-only rule misses more than a third of loop failures the full rule caught, revert to all tools.

idea: Replay the verification step the same way
mechanism: Port the offline-replay method to the harness-run verification part: over the same 40 plus 40 logs, mark each run where the agent claimed done without a real verify step and ask whether a harness-run check at that point would have caught the failure.
prediction: Wrong-verification and some lost-the-goal failures show a claimed-done step without a real test run, while passing runs almost always show one.
test: If passing runs also lack a real verify step in a large share of cases, the harness check cannot separate them and the part is weakened.

idea: Interrupt message pinned to the task
mechanism: Combine the repeated-output rule with task pinning: when the rule fires, the rethink message quotes the pinned task text and the last two differing outputs, so the interrupt cannot itself cause a lost-the-goal failure.
prediction: Among interrupted runs, task-text-in-context-at-end stays yes, and lost-the-goal does not rise, unlike luka's summary experiment.
test: In the 12-task screen, read every interrupted run; if any shows the task text missing after the interrupt, the message design is wrong.

idea: Fire on repeat, then restart instead of rethink
mechanism: Flip the rule that the agent should be told to rethink in place. On the third identical result, end the run and start the retry immediately with the failing output and a one-line note of what was tried, instead of letting the run burn to the cap. The current retry-from-scratch default already shows the second seed often passes.
prediction: Long-task pair pass stays near the retry baseline of 44 percent while cost per failed task falls, because the first attempt stops at the fire step instead of step 60.
test: 12-task screen with the same seeds against the current retry default; refuted if pair pass drops or cost does not fall.
breaks: The rule that the harness interrupts to let the same run recover; here the run is abandoned on first clear loop.
kill: Long-task pair pass more than 3 points below the retry baseline on the full measurement, or cost per task not lower.

idea: Expectation as a required test-tool argument
mechanism: Drops the fixed step 25 trigger. The test-run tool gains a required field "expect" that the agent must fill with a failure count or named test before the tool executes; the harness refuses the call without it and records the field.
prediction: Loop runs fall more than with the step-25 message because the gate fires before every re-run, and the harness gets a gradeable field for free. Cost rises 1 to 3 percent from the extra argument text.
test: Same 12-task screen, 3 seeds, gated tool vs plain tool. Refuted if loop failures are unchanged or the agent fills the field with a constant string on most calls.
part: loop breaking: stop and rethink on repeated cycles

idea: Harness-graded mismatch notice
mechanism: After the checkpoint, the harness compares the stated expected failure count with the actual count from the next test run and, on a mismatch, injects one sentence stating the two numbers. No prescription, in the factual-nudge style.
prediction: Runs that wrote an expectation and then saw it fail change their edit target more often than runs that only wrote it. Loop failures fall by one more run per 9 than write-only.
test: 12-task screen with grading on vs off, checkpoint on in both arms. Refuted if the two arms match on loop failures.
part: loop breaking: stop and rethink on repeated cycles

idea: Single-field checkpoint, next test only
mechanism: Cut the three fields to one: "the next test run will show". Drops confirmed and unknown, which are the fields most likely to become a long summary that eats context.
prediction: Same loop reduction as the three-field version at a third of the token cost, and fewer runs where the agent restarts exploration after reflecting.
test: 12-task screen, one field vs three fields. Refuted if the one-field arm has more loop failures or the same token cost.
part: loop breaking: stop and rethink on repeated cycles

idea: Task restatement at the same checkpoint
mechanism: Reuses the call-25 hook for the lost-the-goal failure kind. The prompt asks the agent to restate the task in one sentence; the harness compares it to the pinned task text by word overlap and re-injects the original text if the overlap is low.
prediction: Lost-the-goal failures, which luka's note says rose under summarisation, fall when the restatement triggers re-injection, with no loop effect.
test: 12-task screen on tasks with lost-the-goal failures in the real data, hook on vs off. Refuted if task-text-in-context at the end is unchanged or lost-the-goal count is flat.
part: keeping the task text pinned so trimming never drops it

idea: Checkpoint carried into the retry
mechanism: Combines the checkpoint with the existing retry default as Reflexion across episodes [F20]. The retry run starts with the first run's checkpoint answers and its last test output as a pinned note, instead of from scratch.
prediction: Pair pass on long tasks rises above the 44 percent retry baseline by 3 to 6 points at about 1 percent more cost, because the second run skips the exploration the first already did.
test: 12-task screen, retry with carried note vs retry from scratch, only on tasks where the first run failed. Refuted if pair pass is flat or the second run repeats the first run's loop.
part: loop breaking: stop and rethink on repeated cycles
breaks: the rule that a retry starts from scratch with no memory of the failed run
kill: pair pass on long tasks below 46 percent in the screen, or cost per task up more than 20 percent

idea: Agent-declared step budget replaces the fixed cap
mechanism: At call 25 the agent states how many more tool calls it needs; the harness sets the cap to that number plus 10, bounded by 60. A run that exceeds its own estimate gets one notice, then stops.
prediction: Loop runs stop earlier than the cap on average, cutting tokens on failed runs by 10 to 30 percent, while passing runs are untouched because they finish within their estimate.
test: 12-task screen, declared budget vs fixed cap of 60. Refuted if long-task pass drops by 2 or more points or failed-run tokens are unchanged.
part: loop breaking: stop and rethink on repeated cycles
breaks: the rule that the step cap is a fixed harness constant the agent never sees
kill: long-task pass down 2 points or more at the screen

idea: Diff against the edit, not the last run
mechanism: Drops the assumption that the agent loops because it cannot see sameness. On a repeated test command the harness shows the file diff since the last run of that command, next to the output diff, so "no files changed since last run" is the literal observation.
prediction: Runs that re-run with no intervening edit fall to near zero; loop cycles per long run drop by half.
test: 12-task screen, 36 runs; refuted if re-runs with an empty file diff persist at baseline rate.

idea: Diff plus mandatory state-change gate
mechanism: When the diff is "0 lines changed" and no file changed since the last run, the harness refuses the second identical command and returns "nothing changed; edit, change the command, or state what you expect to differ".
prediction: Consecutive identical commands cap at 2; loop failures fall by over a third; cost falls.
test: Same screen; refuted if agents evade by adding a no-op flag in over a third of blocked cases.
breaks: The harness only shows results; it never refuses a well-formed tool call.
kill: Long pass gain under 6 points, or short pass down more than 2 points, or flag-evasion rate above one third.

idea: Failing-test-set diff only
mechanism: Instead of a text diff, the harness parses test output into a set of failing test ids and reports only which ids entered or left the set, with the full output for any newly failing test.
prediction: "0 tests changed" appears in most repeated runs; agents never lose an assertion message; tokens per cycle fall by over 80 percent.
test: Replay 50 real baseline test outputs through the parser; refuted if more than 10 percent fail to parse or hide an assertion the agent later used.

idea: Diff view on repeated file reads
mechanism: Port to context trimming. A re-read of a file already in context returns only the diff since the last read, with the raw file only if it was trimmed out.
prediction: Runs that read files over 300 lines twice shrink by 10 percent or more in tokens; stale-context failures do not rise.
test: Screen on tasks with large repeated reads; refuted if stale-context failures rise or tokens fall under 5 percent.

idea: Diff view with Reflexion-style note on mismatch
mechanism: Combine with Reflexion: when the diff contradicts the agent's one-line prediction, the harness asks for a two-line reflection stored in a pinned notes block that survives trimming.
prediction: Reflections appear in the strategy switch in over half of mismatch cases; lost-the-goal failures do not rise.
test: 36-run screen; refuted if reflections are written but the next command is still identical in over half of cases.

idea: Invert the order: prediction required only when the diff is empty
mechanism: Flip the proposal's rule that a prediction precedes every repeated command. Predictions are demanded only after a "0 lines changed" diff, so the cost falls on looping runs only.
prediction: Prediction prompts per run fall to under a third of the always-on rule, with the same or better loop reduction.
test: Compare arms always-predict and predict-on-empty-diff on the 12-task screen; refuted if loop cycles are higher in the gated arm.
breaks: A prediction is required before every repeated command.
kill: Loop cycles per run higher than the always-predict arm, or long pass gain under 6 points.

idea: Harness-prepended task text, no model quote
mechanism: Drop the assumption that the model must quote. The harness builds the summary as the original task message, verbatim and untouched, followed by the model's summary of everything after it. No gate, no retry, no fallback.
prediction: Lost-the-goal failures fall to the no-summariser baseline with zero retry cost; long-task pass matches or beats the gated arm.
test: Third arm in the same 12-task screen. Refuted if the gated arm beats it by more than 2 points on long tasks, which would mean the act of quoting itself helps.
part: task text pinning: keep the goal in the live window

idea: Mechanical content check on the summary body
mechanism: After the TASK slot, the template requires a FILES section; the harness checks that every file path edited in the summarised span, taken from the tool log, appears in that section, and rejects the summary otherwise. The goal and the progress state are both gated by string checks against ground truth the harness already holds.
prediction: Stale-context failures fall further than with the task gate alone, because the summary cannot silently forget which files changed.
test: Two arms, task gate only versus task gate plus FILES gate, on the screen. Refuted if stale-context failures are equal or acceptance drops under 50 percent.
part: task text pinning: keep the goal in the live window

idea: Tail reminder only for the three steps after a summary
mechanism: Immediately after each summary is installed, the harness appends the task text as an ephemeral tail reminder, not written to history, for the next three requests only. This targets the re-orientation moment when the agent first works from a summary rather than its own history.
prediction: Lost-the-goal failures in the steps following a summary fall relative to a head-only summary, at a cost of three short appends per summary.
test: Screen arm versus head-only gated summary. Refuted if lost-the-goal counts are equal.
part: task text pinning: keep the goal in the live window

idea: String-gated final checklist in verification
mechanism: Before the harness accepts a final answer, the agent must emit the task text verbatim followed by one line per requirement marked done or not done. The harness string-matches the quote and refuses to end the run while any line is not done or the quote mismatches, up to the step cap.
prediction: Wrong-verification and lost-the-goal failures at the end of runs fall, because finishing requires re-reading the goal mechanically.
test: Screen arm versus current ending. Refuted if pass is flat or the cap is hit more often with no pass gain.
part: verification: how the agent is told to verify

idea: Event-triggered task re-injection on loop detection
mechanism: Combine the gated summary with event-triggered reminders: when the harness detects the same tool call and arguments twice in a row, or the same failing test three times, it appends the task text plus the line "you have repeated this step" as an ephemeral tail message.
prediction: Loop failures fall alongside lost-the-goal, since the reminder fires only when the agent is already off track, with near-zero cost on healthy runs.
test: Screen arm versus gated summary alone. Refuted if loop failures do not fall or if the detector fires on more than a third of passing runs.
part: loops: detect and break repeated cycles

idea: Task lives in the system prompt, not in history
mechanism: Flip the rule that the task is the first user message. The harness moves the task text into the system prompt at run start and the history begins empty. Trimming and summarising then cannot touch the goal, and the ungated summariser from F14 can be re-run as is.
prediction: Lost-the-goal failures fall to zero by construction; long-task pass rises by more than the +3 of the ungated summariser because its stale-context benefit is kept and its harm removed.
test: Screen arm versus the ungated summariser rerun on the same 12 tasks. Refuted if lost-the-goal is unchanged while the task is provably present, which would confirm presence without influence.
part: task text pinning: keep the goal in the live window
breaks: the rule that the task is a user message and that the system prompt is static across runs
kill: long-task pass on the screen not above the ungated summariser arm by at least 2 points, or short-task pass lower by any amount
